advances: The sharp bound \(|A|+s(A)\le40\) holds for the complete class of rational affine lower and upper slabs over the fixed twenty-point tetrahedron, with every integer fiber nonempty and maximum reflection count at most three. Affinity of both boundaries restores the two-point bound on every nonvertex fiber, despite arbitrary starting heights and parities. This closes this fixed-base construction; it does not give a dimension-growing conclusion or resolve the locked weak Oertel conjecture.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The declared predecessor supplies the fixed base census, its parity classes, the nonvertex midpoint property, and the base reflection counts. All slab inequalities and the uniform exclusion are proved directly above.
proof:
Accepted fact 768d9712b73c4ab7 gives the complete twenty-point census of \(B_{\mathrm{tet}}\), with vertex indices \(0,1,2,19\). It also proves that every other base point is the midpoint of a pair of distinct base points. Its complete base parity classes are as follows:

```text
base parity    census indices
000            0,12,18
001            6,16
010            2,5,8
011            11,14
100            1,4,15
101            10,17
110            9,13,19
111            3,7
```

In particular, there are four classes of size two, all of whose points are nonvertices, and four classes of size three, each consisting of one vertex and two nonvertices. We use precisely these census properties and the predecessor's maximum base reflection count of three.

For each \(p\in B_{\mathrm{tet}}\), let \(L_p=\lceil\ell_-(p)\rceil\), \(U_p=\lfloor\ell_+(p)\rfloor\), and \(m_p=U_p-L_p+1\). The fiber over \(p\) is the integer interval \(\{L_p,\ldots,U_p\}\), and the hypothesis says \(m_p\ge1\). The set \(Q=\{(x,t):x\in P_{\mathrm{tet}},\ \ell_-(x)\le t\le\ell_+(x)\}\) is convex and satisfies \(Q\cap\mathbb Z^4=A\). Thus every integer midpoint of points of \(A\) belongs to \(A\), and every integer center outside \(A\) has reflection count zero. It also follows that \(A=\operatorname{conv}(A)\cap\mathbb Z^4\).

First, \(m_p\le4\) for every base point. Otherwise \((p,L_p+2)\) is the common midpoint of the two distinct vertical unordered pairs with endpoint heights \((L_p,L_p+4)\) and \((L_p+1,L_p+3)\). Together with zero, these give at least five oriented displacements.

Next, \(m_p\le2\) at every nonvertex. To prove this, fix a nonvertex \(p\) and distinct \(q,r\in B_{\mathrm{tet}}\) satisfying \(q+r=2p\), whose existence is supplied by the accepted base certificate. Affinity and the exact ceiling and floor inequalities give

\[
\begin{aligned}
L_q+L_r&<\ell_-(q)+\ell_-(r)+2=2\ell_-(p)+2\le2L_p+2,\\
U_q+U_r&>\ell_+(q)+\ell_+(r)-2=2\ell_+(p)-2\ge2U_p-2.
\end{aligned}
\]

Both sums are integers, so \(L_q+L_r\le2L_p+1\) and \(U_q+U_r\ge2U_p-1\). If \(m_p\ge3\), set \(t=L_p+1\). Then \(L_p<t<U_p\), and

\(L_q+L_r\le2L_p+1<2t<2U_p-1\le U_q+U_r\).

The sums of the two nonempty integer intervals \(\{L_q,\ldots,U_q\}\) and \(\{L_r,\ldots,U_r\}\) fill the entire integer interval \(\{L_q+L_r,\ldots,U_q+U_r\}\). Hence some heights \(u,v\) in those respective fibers satisfy \(u+v=2t\). The center \((p,t)\) therefore has the vertical unordered pair \(\{(p,t-1),(p,t+1)\}\) and the unordered pair \(\{(q,u),(r,v)\}\). The latter has distinct base endpoints and so is different from the vertical pair. Zero and the two pairs give at least five oriented displacements, a contradiction. This proves the nonvertex bound. In particular, it uses both affine boundaries and does not assume a common lower endpoint.

We also need a restriction on two fibers whose base points have the same parity. They cannot have lengths at least three and at least two, respectively. Suppose to the contrary that \(q\ne r\) are in the same base parity class, \(m_q\ge3\), and \(m_r\ge2\). Write \(a=L_q\) and \(b=L_r\). There are two distinct endpoint-height pairs summing to \(a+b+1\), namely \((a,b+1)\) and \((a+1,b)\), and two distinct endpoint-height pairs summing to \(a+b+2\), namely \((a+1,b+1)\) and \((a+2,b)\). All these heights belong to the corresponding fibers. One of these two consecutive sums is even. Its two endpoint-height pairs then give two distinct unordered pairs of points of \(A\) with the same integer midpoint, since \((q+r)/2\) is integral. The unordered pairs are distinct because the base endpoints \(q,r\) are distinct. The midpoint belongs to \(A\) by convexity, so its zero displacement and these two pairs give reflection count at least five. This contradiction proves the restriction, for arbitrary starting heights and parities.

For each base parity class, let \(N_0,N_1\) be the numbers of points in its two lifted ambient parity classes, distinguished by the parity of the fourth coordinate. Its contribution to \(|A|+s(A)\) is exactly \(N_0+\mathbf1_{\{N_0=1\}}+N_1+\mathbf1_{\{N_1=1\}}\). These contributions partition all sixteen ambient parity classes.

In a base class of size two, both fiber lengths are at most two by the nonvertex bound. An integer interval of length at most two contributes at most one point to each height parity. Thus \(0\le N_0,N_1\le2\). For every integer \(N\in\{0,1,2\}\), one has \(N+\mathbf1_{\{N=1\}}\le2\), so this base class contributes at most four.

Consider a base class of size three. If its vertex fiber also has length at most two, every fiber contributes at most one point to each height parity, so \(0\le N_0,N_1\le3\). The inequality \(N+\mathbf1_{\{N=1\}}\le3\) for every integer \(N\in\{0,1,2,3\}\) gives a contribution at most six.

If the vertex fiber has length three or four, the restriction on same-parity fibers forces each of its two nonvertex class mates to have length one. With vertex length three, there are five points in total, and both lifted parity classes are nonempty because three consecutive integers contain both parities. At most one of the two lifted classes is a singleton, so the contribution is at most six. With vertex length four, there are six points in total, and the vertex fiber alone gives two points of each height parity. Neither lifted class is a singleton, so the contribution is exactly six.

There are four base classes of each size. Adding the proved bounds yields \(|A|+s(A)\le4\cdot4+4\cdot6=40\). No coefficient bound, denominator bound, or parameter enumeration has been used; the proof covers every rational affine pair in the statement.

Finally, take \(\ell_-=0\) and \(\ell_+=1\). Then \(A=B_{\mathrm{tet}}\times\{0,1\}\) and \(|A|=40\). Every lifted parity class has the same size, two or three, as its base class, so \(s(A)=0\). At a supported center, a reflected pair in the fourth coordinate \(\{0,1\}\) has zero displacement in that coordinate. Thus its reflection count is exactly the base reflection count, which is at most three by accepted fact 768d9712b73c4ab7. Centers outside \(A\) have count zero as already proved. This gives equality and verifies sharpness within the required class.
statement:
Let \(P_{\mathrm{tet}}=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(31,53,78)\}\) and \(B_{\mathrm{tet}}=P_{\mathrm{tet}}\cap\mathbb Z^3\). The alias map from accepted fact 768d9712b73c4ab7 is \(P\mapsto P_{\mathrm{tet}}\) and its three-dimensional support \(A\mapsto B_{\mathrm{tet}}\). Its census indices \(p_0,\ldots,p_{19}\) are unchanged. The symbol \(A\) below denotes the new four-dimensional slab.

Let \(\ell_-,\ell_+:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R\) be arbitrary rational affine functions satisfying \(\ell_-(x)\le\ell_+(x)\) for all \(x\in P_{\mathrm{tet}}\). Put

\(A=\{(p,t)\in\mathbb Z^4:p\in B_{\mathrm{tet}},\ \ell_-(p)\le t\le\ell_+(p)\}\).

Assume that every \(p\in B_{\mathrm{tet}}\) has a nonempty integer fiber. For \(w\in\mathbb Z^4\), define \(r_A(w)=|\{v\in\mathbb Z^4:w+v,w-v\in A\}|\), with oriented displacements and zero included exactly once at a supported center. Let \(s(A)\) count the classes in the ambient quotient \(\mathbb Z^4/2\mathbb Z^4\) containing exactly one point of \(A\). If \(r_A(w)\le3\) for every \(w\in\mathbb Z^4\), then \(|A|+s(A)\le40\). Equality is attained by \(\ell_-=0\) and \(\ell_+=1\).
